confirmatory_design.fold0: DEVELOPMENT -- excluded from every headline number
confirmatory_design.note: this file must exist and be hashed BEFORE any confirmatory fold runs

grounds.summary: DECLARED ON COST, NOT DERIVED FROM THE CURVE. The fold-0 development curve does not locate a budget, so no budget in 250-8000 is defensible over any other on evidence. The choice is therefore an explicit cost decision and is labelled as one.
grounds.what_would_falsify_this_choice: a confirmatory fold whose own curve showed a decay this fold-0 curve does not. That cannot be checked without breaking the pre-registration, and it is the accepted residual risk of the 7.14 protocol -- stated in 7.14 itself: 'if every method's development curve is equally unlocatable, the procedure is principled machinery wrapped around a coin flip. It remains fair, but it is not precise, and the paper must say so.'
why_not_derived: the Task-A decay detector, applied UNMODIFIED (same definition, same sha256, same bootstrap, same cap), returns Delta = +0.027806 with 95% CI [-0.014372, +0.070153] -- NOT DISTINGUISHABLE. There is no systematic 'late is worse' structure to shorten the budget against, which is what 7.14 predicted for a method with no pseudo-label loop.

pairwise across all 496 candidate-budget comparisons, 69 are distinguishable at an UNCORRECTED 95% against 24.8 expected under a global null, and 8 survive Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.05. This does NOT repeat 7.13's 0-of-24.

but every surviving pair is a PEAK-vs-TROUGH pair of a wobbling curve, not evidence about when to stop: they include step 5000 vs step 5750, 750 steps apart in mid-run, and they cluster on the curve's extremes (the six most-involved steps are [[1500, 18], [7750, 14], [2500, 13], [2250, 11], [4000, 9], [5750, 8]], headed by the curve minimum 0.3163 at step 1500 and the maximum 0.5306 at step 2500). A curve whose neighbouring points differ by more than the resolution is noisy, not locatable.
the argmax (step 2500) is NOT distinguishable from step 2000 (diff +0.0612, CI [-0.0102, +0.1531]), and its edge over the endpoint (p=0.0152) does NOT survive the multiplicity correction.

the known-null half-width -- the same checkpoint against itself under independent resamples -- is 0.1633, against a total curve range of 0.2143. Unpaired, the entire curve barely clears the noise floor.
why_this_value: COST. Measured 298.08 min for 8000 steps on a Kaggle T4 (231 min training + 67 min scoring 32 checkpoints). At 2000 steps a confirmatory fold is ~75 min, so folds 1-4 cost ~5 GPU-hours against ~20 at 8000. With nothing distinguishable, a 4x cost multiple buys nothing measurable.

NOT THE ARGMAX. Step 2500 is the maximum of a curve whose distinguishable pairs are peak-vs-trough, so selecting it is winner's curse. 7.11 set this precedent explicitly when it declined to pin FreeMatch's budget to its own argmax at 1250.

step 2000 is additionally the one point on this curve whose model is INDEPENDENTLY CHARACTERISED: the 2000-step gamma=16 sweep arm, which this run reproduced bit-exactly on all 11 logged columns across all 2000 steps. That is a provenance convenience, NOT evidence that 2000 is a better budget than any other.

method: deep_coral, n_blocks=3, image-space, gamma=16, target EMA off
metric: TPR@FPR=1e-3 as a RATE (PROJECT.md 2/9); never counts. One positive = 0.010204 on 98 fold positives against 26399 shared negatives.
purpose: PRE-REGISTRATION for the CORAL confirmatory folds 1-4 (PROJECT.md 7.14). The budget and the read-off point are fixed HERE, before any confirmatory fold exists. Fold 0 is DEVELOPMENT and contributes no headline number.
read_off_rule: train to step 2000 and read the FINAL checkpoint (step_2000.pt). This is R1 -- the last checkpoint -- as pre-registered throughout the project. No label-free selector, no argmax, no smoothing, no re-reading at another step: THE BUDGET IS THE SELECTOR.

task2_pairwise.freematch_precedent: §7.13: 0 of 24 candidate budgets in 500-3375 distinguishable from the best

task3_known_null.scheme: same checkpoint, two INDEPENDENT resample streams (seeds 0 and 1); the paired scheme gives identically zero
